findings.finding: The 700,000 / six million / 2.2 million peak figures are made to fall under 'by Hachtmann's caveat'. In #1669 they are not Hachtmann's. The ledger gives them as #1669's own statement, and #1669 sources them to Spoerer (§3.4, §6.6, note 6). Hachtmann's caveat (Z1669-53) is only the minority and the 1942–44 span.
findings.evidence: Z1669-57 quote: "Camp prisoners were a small part of the foreign labor force: about 700,000 against about six million civilians and 2.2 million prisoners of war at the peak." #1669 §3.4: "At the late-war peak about nine million foreign workers and prisoners were present at once: about six million civilians, 2.2 million prisoners of war and about 700,000 camp prisoners.[^6]" (note 6 = Spoerer 2008)
findings.fix: Split the clause: "...for by Hachtmann's caveat only a minority of camp prisoners was used in industrial production, from late 1942 to mid-1944; camp prisoners, #1669 states, were a small part of the foreign labor force, about 700,000 against about six million civilians and 2.2 million prisoners of war at the peak;..."

findings.where: P section 'Conquest as labor', item 'People, not land:'
findings.finding: The label makes #1669 say people instead of land. #1669 says land and then people: the empire for land also became a labor supply. The label pushes the archive's claim past its own wording, which is a raised force (§4.4, §5.3).
findings.evidence: Z1669-19: "Lebensraum answered with land. What conquest delivered to the factory, from 1940 onward, was people. Labor became a binding constraint, and the empire pursued for land, settlement and racial reordering also became a mechanism for supplying it."
findings.fix: Label 'Land, then people:' with text "Lebensraum answered with land; what conquest delivered to the factory from 1940 was people (#1669)."

findings.where: KO sentence 23; P section 'Why Germany lost', item 'Conquest unpaid:'; open item 3
findings.finding: The KO keeps only the first part of Z1669-80, 'not necessarily representative cases'. It drops the part that matters most: involvement in the system often had political and social causes, not only economic ones. Z1669-81 (value explains why a firm took prisoners, access explains which firms got them) rests on that part, so as composed Z1669-81 follows from nothing. In P, 'forced labor often did not pay' loses the representativeness limit altogether.
findings.evidence: Z1669-80 quote: "These are not necessarily representative cases, but they point to something important: involvement in the slave labor system frequently had political and social causes rather than exclusively economic ones."
findings.fix: KO 23: "...calling these 'not necessarily representative cases' that show involvement in the slave labor system 'frequently had political and social causes rather than exclusively economic ones', and #1669 holds that value explains why a firm took prisoners and access explains which firms got them." P: "forced labor in many cases did not pay for itself, in cases Hayes calls not necessarily representative (Hayes, via #1669)."

findings.finding: The KO quotes only the last clause of the tribunal's finding. It drops the tribunal's own limit, that the camp may not have been the deciding factor in choosing the site. This is 'limit dropped': the clause carries more than the tribunal found.
findings.evidence: Z1669-59 quote: "while the camp may not have been the determining factor in selecting the location, it was an important one and, from the beginning, it was planned to use concentration-camp labor to supplement the supply of workers."
findings.fix: "at Auschwitz the IG Farben tribunal found the camp, though perhaps not the determining factor in the choice of site, 'an important one', and that 'from the beginning, it was planned to use concentration-camp labor to supplement the supply of workers'"

findings.finding: The KO ends with four archive-only sentences: the Holocaust limit and the non-claims, colonial continuity, Arendt's frame, and the EVZ payments with the source grades and relations. They come after the field-only defeat cluster (22, 24), so the KO closes with the archive as a block. That is the shape §4.1 rules out in the equal-terms case. The order does not come from dependency. #1669 says its Holocaust limit 'governs §9', which is the material of KO 20–21. Colonial continuity and Arendt's frame belong to the colony sense in KO 9 (Z1669-11 is already there) and KO 11. Sentences 1–24 interleave well; only the tail is a block.
findings.evidence: Z1669-14: "The Holocaust is larger than this labor history. That limit governs §9." Z1669-11: "The colonial reading of Nazism has three parts... (a) The East as colonial empire is the least contested." (parts b and c are composed only in KO 25–26)
findings.fix: Put KO 25 straight after KO 21, so the limit closes the annihilation sense. Put KO 26 after KO 9, completing the three-part colonial reading. Put KO 27 after KO 11, or join it to 'the colony entered the factory'. Keep the defeat cluster (22–24) as the close, with KO 28's source grades and relations either folded into the sentences they grade or kept last as a short apparatus sentence. Log these moves as coordinating acts (§4.7).

findings.finding: The lede names a source only for the archive claim (#1669). The field claims F1 (war state, invasion of Poland) and F34 (caused in part by the Depression and First World War tensions) appear with no source, against §4.5. findings.evidence: Lede: "is that of a Nazi war state's war of conquest, begun by invading Poland in 1939 and caused in part by the Depression and tensions left by the First World War; that state was ... (#1669)."
findings.fix: "is that of a Nazi war state's war of conquest, begun by invading Poland in 1939 (National WWII Museum) and caused in part by the Depression and tensions left by the First World War (History.com); that state was an advanced industrial power for which labor became a binding wartime constraint, and its land program, Lebensraum, was turned in practice into a labor supply (#1669)."

case_reasoning: ρ = extends, equal-terms case, agreed. #1669 §0.8 accepts the conventional reading (§0.1–0.7) whole and names its object as an addition on the field's own entity: the form of the labor relation. Its senses rest on field scholarship it reports (Herbert, Hachtmann, Spoerer, Hayes, Nelson, USHMM). §9.7 gives the field's own name for its central tension (Hayes's 'mutually negating desires'). §11.5 calls the paper an extension of Arendt's frame. §12 ¶2 states its non-claims, so nothing in the field's ontology is contested. The witness case needs an ontology no other source makes available; the paper itself shows the field already holds this one. A reader of the same two papers would decide the same way.
summary: Equal-terms case and ρ = extends are supported by verbatim loci and agreed. Coverage, kernels, translation verbatim-ness and the opening-run check all pass. Nine should-fix items: the 700,000 peak figure credited to Hachtmann instead of Spoerer (C1); 'People, not land' raising Z1669-19 (C2); Hayes's political-causes limit dropped (C3); the tribunal's 'not the determining factor' dropped (C4); the KO closing with four archive-only sentences that belong with the annihilation and colony senses (C5); the P lede missing field attribution (C6); the garbled 'Relocated' item (C7); 'annihilation through labor' unattributed in P (C8); Z1669-11 unattributed in KO 9 (C9). Twelve notes.
